title: Keyword Search Is Dying. Is Your Catalog Ready for AI Agents? — PayPal
talk_summary: A PayPal product director argues commerce is shifting from keyword search to intent/semantic search driven by AI agents, and that merchant catalogs must be enriched to be discoverable by agents. They ran enrichment experiments and found structured, quality content improves agent recommendations while over-enrichment and boilerplate dilute signal and increase hallucination.

takeaways.evidence_quote: more text isn't better. um structured quality content, structured quality content is the one thing that wins out
takeaways.numbers: Unenriched baseline 'completely underperformed' head-to-head; thinnest catalogs gained most

takeaways.what_they_do: They found that injecting too much meaning/context can lose focus and cause the agent to hallucinate and underperform.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when we overenriched the agent tended to hallucinate more and it underperformed

takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than guessing, they ran controlled experiments comparing enriched vs unenriched data against agent recommendations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we ran experiments to see how agents uh uh searched uh and and recommended products

takeaways.what_they_do: They combine precise literal keyword matching with fuzzy semantic retrieval because each alone fails (keyword misses intent, semantic loses focus).
takeaways.evidence_quote: the real answer isn't an either or. It's it's combining both, which is exactly what our hybrid approach does
